newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-TWO-GOAL VAN HOOIJDONK GIVES DUTCH WINNING START.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-TWO-GOAL VAN HOOIJDONK GIVES DUTCH WINNING START.

text.p: Substitute Pierre Van Hooijdonk struck twice in three minutes to lead the Netherlands to a 3-1 victory over Wales in their World Cup opener on Saturday.
The Celtic striker fired a 72nd minute equaliser with his first touch then swept home a second on the break to turn the European group seven qualifier on its head.
Ronald De Boer added a third goal with 11 minutes remaining with a diving header from Philip Cocu's cross.
Wales had high hopes of maintaining their 100 percent record when Dean Saunders put them ahead on 17 minutes.
But the Dutch hit back strongly and although goalkeeper Neville Southall kept Wales ahead with a string of brilliant saves, the overwhelming pressure told in the end.
Wales, with two big wins against San Marino behind them, had hoped that the Dutch would be vulnerable after a traumatic Euro 96 and a rash of injuries that forced them to field a weakened side.
Southall made a vital save 15 minutes into the game when Jordi Cruyff was sent clear, blocking the Manchester United forward's shot with his legs.

But Wales were ahead within two minutes with skipper Barry Horne the provider. He burst into the Dutch penalty area and, although his initial shot was blocked, he collected the rebound, drew Edwin Van Der Sar and squared for Saunders to walk the ball into an empty net.

The Dutch piled on the pressure after the break and at the height of their siege, Southall made three stunning saves in as many minutes to deny substitute Roy Makaay, Ronald De Boer and Clarence Seedorf.
But an equaliser seemed inevitable and once Van Hooijdonk supplied it the Dutch cut loose.
Wales - Southall, Bowen, Pembridge (Legg 65), Browning (Jenkins 83), Melville, Symons, Horne, Robinson, Saunders, Hughes, Speed.
Netherlands - Van der Sar, Vierklau (Van Hooijdonk 70), Valckx, F. De Boer, Bogarde, Jonk, Winter, Cruyff (Makaay 46), R. De Boer (Van Bronckhurst 89), Seedorf, Cocu.
